messages:
ejordan: Quick follow-up on decomposed authz for Private CP endpoints — RFC flagged two options: delegated token-exchange (OIDC/STs) vs client-cert mTLS. Want to capture tradeoffs and a pragmatic fallback for air-gapped customers. Thoughts?

maria: Can you call out the concrete flows you expect? e.g., tenant agent -> CP control plane, or cross-account peering?

ejordan: Mainly tenant agent -> control plane endpoints in customer VPC. Two variants: 1) CP validates short-lived JWTs issued by tenant IDP (token-exchange), 2) CP validates client TLS certs provisioned/rotated per-tenant. Also consider an ops-minted cert fallback for customers without IDP.

ravi: High level pros: tokens = smaller surface to expose, easier to integrate with existing IDPs, key rotation handled by IDP (via JWKS). Cons: need token revocation / short TTLs, clock sync, and JWKS caching complexity. mTLS = strong cryptographic binding and offline-friendly if certs pre-provisioned. Ops burden for issuance/rotation is nontrivial.

katie: For mTLS we also need KMS/HSM integration for signing keys or a CA service. If we go full-ops CA we inherit cert lifecycle support and audit burden. Air-gapped customers hate outbound calls, so certs are attractive there.

sebastian: Suggest hybrid: primary path = token-exchange (OIDC token exchange to mint CP-scoped token). Fallback path = pre-provisioned client cert bundle + CRL/OCSP checks when connectivity exists. Example token flow:
```
# tenant -> idp exchange (pseudo)
POST https://tenant-idp.local/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange&subject_token=<agent-token>&requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token
```
CP validates returned JWT against tenant JWKS, checks scope claim (e.g., cp:agent:connect) and tenant-id. JWKS cache TTL ~5m.

defense: cache poisoning risk and jwks rotation spikes during rollout.

infra-bot: deploy: authn-proxy v2 was rolled to staging (canary) with jwks-cache TTL support. :white_check_mark:

ravi: Two more failure modes: a) IDP outage -> agents can't get tokens (but can use cached token until expiry), b) clock drift -> token rejected. We can mitigate with short TTL + token refresh jitter and NTP enforcement in agent.

katie: For air-gapped we can allow operator-provisioned certs via a signed bundle uploaded to customer CP. But that needs a secure upload UX + tooling to rotate certs. Could do an "operator-issue certs" mode where operator CA signs per-tenant leaf certs and the agent auto-rotates.

sebastian: Another middle ground: use attestation tokens minted locally by the agent, signed with a device key provisioned during onboarding (hardware-backed if available). CP verifies attestation signature and then issues a CP-scoped short-lived token. That reduces dependency on external IDP on first connect.

maria: Are there regulatory concerns? e.g., customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed keys? If we do operator CA or KMS for certs, that may not be acceptable for some enterprises. Need explicit opt-in options documented.

ejordan: Good point. We should support 3 modes: "tenant-idp" (recommended), "customer-operator-cert" (enterprise opt-in), and "ephemeral-onboard-attest" (air-gap-friendly). Each mode defines: issuance, revocation, audit logging, onboarding UX, rotation cadence.

ravi: Implementation plan I propose: spike to add token-exchange validation path in control plane + JWKS caching (2d); parallel spike for agent-side ACME-like cert minting workflow (3d). Then a short security review.

katie: Also add a matrix in RFC: offline-ability, revocation latency, operational complexity, auditability, KMS requirements, customer opt-in friction.

sebastian: Minor nit: scope model should be per-route and include nonce-bound attestation for long-lived connections (we should avoid wide "cp:*" tokens). Also log token-subject and thumbprint for replay detection.

ejordan: Action items: create follow-up RFC with the 3 modes + matrix and assign spikes. I'll open the RFC by EOD and tag @ravi @katie for spikes. If we prefer air-gap-first customers we default to cert-bundle fallback.

infra-bot: created: RFC 2026 "private-cp-authz-modes" (link: https://go/rfc/2026) assigned: ejordan, ravi, katie.

maria: :thumbsup: + please include migration plan for existing private endpoints.

ejordan: Will do. Thanks all. :clap:
